subject: science
passage: Nineteenth-century naturalists puzzled over erratics, large boulders resting far from any outcrop of the same rock. A popular explanation held that icebergs had rafted them across a once-submerged landscape. That account could explain how the boulders traveled, but it was hard pressed to explain the long parallel grooves cut into the bedrock beneath many of them, marks that suggested something heavy dragged steadily across solid ground. Louis Agassiz, who had studied active glaciers in the Alps, argued that only moving ice sheets could leave such a pattern, and in time the grooves came to be seen not as a difficulty for the glacial theory but as its most ______ support.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The grooves were what the iceberg theory "was hard pressed to explain," and Agassiz argued that "only moving ice sheets" could make them. The phrase "not as a difficulty ... but as" reverses their role: they became strong evidence for the glacial theory. "Persuasive" means convincing.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Peripheral support would be minor, but the grooves are presented as the central evidence for the theory.
explanation.B: Correct. Marks that only moving ice could make became the most convincing evidence for the glacial theory.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Equivocal support would be unclear or open to two readings, but the text says "only moving ice sheets" could leave the grooves.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the grooves were temporary support; "in time" they came to be seen as strong evidence.
